BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2016_012_05.q: Siya buys 11 stickers at 25 rupees each. What is the total cost?
hints: Every sticker costs the same, so this is a multiplication problem. The total cost is the price of one item times the number of items.
Multiply 25 by 11. A handy way is to find 10 lots of 25 first and then add 1 more lot.
Here is a similar one: 12 pencils at 20 rupees each. 10 times 20 equals 200 and 2 times 20 equals 40, so the total is 200 plus 40 equals 240, which is 240 rupees.
steps: Each sticker costs 25 rupees and Siya buys 11 of them, so multiply 25 by 11.
Split 11 into 10 and 1. 10 times 25 equals 250 and 1 times 25 equals 25.
Add the two parts: 250 plus 25 equals 275. 25 times 11 equals 275.
The total cost is 275 rupees.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2016_016_05.q: Siddharth buys 12 erasers at 15 rupees each. What is the total cost?
hints: Every eraser costs the same, so this is a multiplication problem. The total cost is the price of one item times the number of items.
Multiply 15 by 12. You can split 12 into 10 and 2, multiply each part by 15, and add the results.
Here is a similar one: 13 balloons at 12 rupees each. 10 times 12 equals 120 and 3 times 12 equals 36, so the total is 120 plus 36 equals 156, which is 156 rupees.
steps: Each eraser costs 15 rupees and Siddharth buys 12 of them, so multiply 15 by 12.
Split 12 into 10 and 2. 10 times 15 equals 150 and 2 times 15 equals 30.
Add the two parts: 150 plus 30 equals 180. 15 times 12 equals 180.
The total cost is 180 rupees.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2017_021_05.q: Isha buys 10 pens at 10 rupees each. What is the total cost?
hints: Every pen costs the same, so this is a multiplication problem. The total cost is the price of one item times the number of items.
Multiply the price of one pen by the number of pens. Multiplying a number by 10 moves each digit one place to the left and puts a 0 in the ones place.
Here is a similar one: 7 erasers at 10 rupees each cost 7 times 10 equals 70, which is 70 rupees.
steps: Each pen costs 10 rupees and Isha buys 10 of them, so multiply 10 by 10.
Ten tens make one hundred. 10 times 10 equals 100.
The total cost is 100 rupees.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2017_021_07.q: Neha buys a book for 60 rupees and sells it at a profit of 10 percent. What is the selling price?
hints: Find 10 percent of the cost price first.
Selling price equals cost price plus profit.
Profit equals 10 over 100, times 60.
steps: The profit is 10 percent of 60 rupees, which is 6 rupees.
Selling price equals cost price plus profit. That is 60 plus 6, which equals 66 rupees.

hints: This sum mixes division, addition and multiplication. The order matters: division and multiplication are done before addition.
Work out the division 20 divided by 2 and the multiplication 4 times 2 separately first. Then add the two results.
Here is a similar one: 24 divided by 4 plus 5 times 3. First 24 divided by 4 equals 6 and 5 times 3 equals 15. Then 6 plus 15 equals 21.
steps: Do the division first. 20 divided by 2 equals 10.
Do the multiplication next. 4 times 2 equals 8.
Now add the two results: 10 plus 8 equals 18. So 20 divided by 2 plus 4 times 2 equals 18.

hints: This sum has an addition and a multiplication. Multiplication is done before addition, even when the addition is written first.
Work out 6 times 7 first. Then add that result to 43.
Here is a similar one: 25 plus 4 times 9. First 4 times 9 equals 36. Then 25 plus 36 equals 61.
steps: Multiply first, even though the addition is written first. 6 times 7 equals 42.
Now add: 43 plus 42 equals 85.
So 43 plus 6 times 7 equals 85.

hints: This sum has subtraction, multiplication and addition. Multiplication is done first; after that, addition and subtraction are done from left to right.
Work out 4 times 7 first. Then go from left to right: take that result away from 44, and add 2 last.
Here is a similar one: 50 minus 6 times 5 plus 4. First 6 times 5 equals 30. Then 50 minus 30 equals 20, and 20 plus 4 equals 24.
steps: Multiply first. 4 times 7 equals 28.
Now go from left to right. Subtract first. 44 minus 28 equals 16.
Then add the 2. 16 plus 2 equals 18.
So 44 minus 4 times 7 plus 2 equals 18.

hints: This sum has a multiplication and a subtraction. Multiplication is done before subtraction.
Work out 27 times 2 first. Then take 15 away from that result.
Here is a similar one: 34 times 2 minus 18. First 34 times 2 equals 68. Then 68 minus 18 equals 50.
steps: Multiply first. 27 times 2 equals 54.
Now subtract: 54 minus 15 equals 39.
So 27 times 2 minus 15 equals 39.

hints: This sum has subtraction, multiplication and addition. Multiplication is done first; after that, addition and subtraction are done from left to right.
Work out 3 times 5 first. Then go from left to right: take that result away from 63, and add 1 last.
Here is a similar one: 70 minus 8 times 5 plus 3. First 8 times 5 equals 40. Then 70 minus 40 equals 30, and 30 plus 3 equals 33.
steps: Multiply first. 3 times 5 equals 15.
Now go from left to right. Subtract first. 63 minus 15 equals 48.
Then add the 1. 48 plus 1 equals 49.
So 63 minus 3 times 5 plus 1 equals 49.

hints: This sum has a multiplication and an addition. Multiplication is done before addition.
Work out 7 times 7 first. Then add 4 to that result.
Here is a similar one: 8 times 8 plus 3. First 8 times 8 equals 64. Then 64 plus 3 equals 67.
steps: Multiply first. 7 times 7 equals 49.
Now add: 49 plus 4 equals 53.
So 7 times 7 plus 4 equals 53.

hints: This sum has a multiplication and an addition. Multiplication is done before addition.
Work out 22 times 9 first. You can split 22 into 20 and 2 to make it easier. Then add 10 to the result.
Here is a similar one: 15 times 6 plus 20. First 15 times 6 equals 90. Then 90 plus 20 equals 110.
steps: Multiply first. Split 22 into 20 and 2: 20 times 9 equals 180 and 2 times 9 equals 18, and 180 plus 18 equals 198. 22 times 9 equals 198.
Now add: 198 plus 10 equals 208.
So 22 times 9 plus 10 equals 208.

hints: This sum has an addition and a multiplication. Multiplication is done before addition, even when the addition is written first.
Work out 8 times 2 first. Then add that result to 41.
Here is a similar one: 52 plus 9 times 4. First 9 times 4 equals 36. Then 52 plus 36 equals 88.
steps: Multiply first, even though the addition is written first. 8 times 2 equals 16.
Now add: 41 plus 16 equals 57.
So 41 plus 8 times 2 equals 57.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2024_014_05.q: Rohan buys 8 books at 3 rupees each. What is the total cost?
hints: Every book costs the same, so this is a multiplication problem. The total cost is the price of one item times the number of items.
Multiply the price of one book by the number of books. This is a fact from the 3 times table.
Here is a similar one: 6 toys at 7 rupees each cost 6 times 7 equals 42, which is 42 rupees.
steps: Each book costs 3 rupees and Rohan buys 8 of them, so multiply 3 by 8.
Eight threes are twenty-four. 3 times 8 equals 24.
The total cost is 24 rupees.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2024_040_05.q: Karan buys 4 stickers at 15 rupees each. What is the total cost?
hints: Every sticker costs the same, so this is a multiplication problem. The total cost is the price of one item times the number of items.
Multiply 15 by 4. You can split 15 into 10 and 5, multiply each part by 4, and add the results.
Here is a similar one: 5 badges at 14 rupees each. 5 times 10 equals 50 and 5 times 4 equals 20, so the total is 50 plus 20 equals 70, which is 70 rupees.
steps: Each sticker costs 15 rupees and Karan buys 4 of them, so multiply 15 by 4.
Split 15 into 10 and 5. 4 times 10 equals 40 and 4 times 5 equals 20.
Add the two parts: 40 plus 20 equals 60. 15 times 4 equals 60.
The total cost is 60 rupees.

BOOST_EXT_G4_FP_2024_040_07.q: Riya bought a bicycle for 500 rupees and sold it at a loss of 25 percent. What is the selling price?
hints: Find 25 percent of the cost price.
Selling price equals cost price minus loss.
Loss means sold for less than bought.
steps: The loss is 25 percent of 500 rupees, which is 125 rupees.
Selling price equals cost price minus loss. That is 500 minus 125, which equals 375 rupees.

EXT_G4_FP_2020_004.q: Value of open curly bracket, open bracket, 2 plus 3, close bracket, times 5, close curly bracket, minus open bracket, 2 plus 3 times 5, close bracket?
hints: This is an order of operations problem. Brackets come first, and inside a bracket multiplication comes before addition.
Work out each part on its own. In the first part, add 2 plus 3 before you multiply. In the second part there is no inner bracket, so multiply 3 times 5 before you add.

Here is a similar one: open curly bracket, open bracket, 1 plus 4, close bracket, times 3, close curly bracket, minus open bracket, 1 plus 4 times 3, close bracket. The first part is 5 times 3, which is 15. The second part is 1 plus 12, which is 13. Then 15 minus 13 equals 2.
steps: First part: do the inner bracket, then multiply. Open bracket, 2 plus 3, close bracket, times 5, equals 25.
Second part: multiply first, then add. 2 plus 3 times 5 equals 17.
Subtract the second part from the first. 25 minus 17 equals 8.
The value is 8.

EXT_G4_FP_2020_024.q: BODMAS: 13, minus 2 times 3, plus 15 divided by 3.
hints: This sum mixes four operations. Multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction.
Find the multiplication and the division in the sum and work those two out first. Then go from left to right with what is left.
Here is a similar one: 30, minus 4 times 5, plus 18 divided by 6. First 4 times 5 equals 20 and 18 divided by 6 equals 3. Then 30 minus 20 equals 10, and 10 plus 3 equals 13.
steps: Do the multiplication first. 2 times 3 equals 6.
Do the division next. 15 divided by 3 equals 5.
The sum is now 13 minus 6 plus 5. Go from left to right: 13 minus 6 equals 7, and then 7 plus 5 equals 12. 13 minus 6 plus 5 equals 12.
So 13, minus 2 times 3, plus 15 divided by 3, equals 12.

EXT_G4_FP_2020_030.q: Insert sign: 2 plus 3 times 2, blank, 2 times open bracket, 3 plus 2, close bracket.
hints: Work out the value of each side on its own, using the order of operations. Then compare the two values.
On the left there are no brackets, so multiply 3 times 2 before adding. On the right, do the bracket first.

Here is a similar one: 3 plus 2 times 4 and 4 times open bracket, 2 plus 3, close bracket. The left side is 3 plus 8, which is 11. The right side is 4 times 5, which is 20. Since 11 is less than 20, the sign is less than.
steps: Left side: multiply first, then add. 2 plus 3 times 2 equals 8.
Right side: bracket first, then multiply. 2 times open bracket, 3 plus 2, close bracket, equals 10.
8 is less than 10, so the sign is less than.

EXT_G4_FP_2021_033.q: Raunak buys 12 dozen, Shail buys 5 score. Who has more and by how much?
hints: Dozen and score are names for groups. Change both amounts into plain numbers so that you can compare them.
One dozen is 12 and one score is 20. Multiply to find how many each child has.
Here is a similar one. Mira has 6 dozen, which is 6 times 12, or 72. Jay has 3 score, which is 3 times 20, or 60. Mira has more, by 72 minus 60, which is 12.
steps: One dozen is 12, and Raunak has 12 dozen. 12 times 12 equals 144.
One score is 20, and Shail has 5 score. 5 times 20 equals 100.
Raunak has more. Subtract to find how many more. 144 minus 100 equals 44.
Raunak has more, by 44.

EXT_G4_FP_2021_039.q: BODMAS: 7, plus 9 times 3, minus 8 divided by 2?
hints: This sum mixes four operations. Multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction.
Find the multiplication and the division in the sum and work those two out first. Then go from left to right with what is left.
Here is a similar one: 5, plus 6 times 2, minus 9 divided by 3. First 6 times 2 equals 12 and 9 divided by 3 equals 3. Then 5 plus 12 equals 17, and 17 minus 3 equals 14.
steps: Do the multiplication first. 9 times 3 equals 27.
Do the division next. 8 divided by 2 equals 4.
The sum is now 7 plus 27 minus 4. Go from left to right: 7 plus 27 equals 34, and then 34 minus 4 equals 30. 7 plus 27 minus 4 equals 30.
So 7, plus 9 times 3, minus 8 divided by 2, equals 30.

EXT_G4_FP_2022_001.q: BODMAS: 5, box, 3, box, 7, box, 6, equals 20. Insert correct operations.
hints: You have to find which signs make the sum equal 20. Test each set of signs, using the order of operations.
Take one set of signs, put it into the boxes and work it out, doing times and divide before plus and minus. If it does not give 20, try another set.
Here is a similar one: 4, box, 2, box, 5, box, 3, equals 11. Try plus, times and minus. That gives 4 plus 2 times 5 minus 3, equals 4 plus 10 minus 3, which equals 11, so those signs fit.
steps: Try the signs plus, times and minus. Multiply first. 3 times 7 equals 21.
Then add and subtract from left to right. 5 plus 21 minus 6 equals 20.
The signs plus, times and minus make the sum equal 20.

EXT_G4_FP_2022_007.q: Bracket in 17 minus 8 times 4 plus 5 equals 41?
hints: A bracket changes which part is done first. Test each bracket and see which one makes the sum equal 41.
Take one of the brackets, put it into 17 minus 8 times 4 plus 5 and work it out, bracket first. If it does not give 41, try another.

Here is a similar one. Where does a bracket go to make 12 minus 2 times 3 plus 1 equal to 31? Try a bracket around 12 minus 2. Then 10 times 3 plus 1, equals 30 plus 1, which equals 31, so that bracket fits.
steps: Try a bracket around 17 minus 8 and do it first. 17 minus 8 equals 9.
Multiply next. 9 times 4 equals 36.
Then add. 36 plus 5 equals 41.
The bracket goes around 17 minus 8.

EXT_G4_FP_2022_025.q: Bananas sold at 30 rupees for half dozen. How many for 85 rupees?
hints: First find the price of one banana. Then see how many bananas the money will buy.
Half a dozen is 6 bananas. Divide 30 rupees by 6 to get the price of one banana.
Here is a similar one. Half a dozen mangoes cost 48 rupees. One mango costs 48 divided by 6, which is 8 rupees. For 72 rupees you get 72 divided by 8, which is 9 mangoes.
steps: Half a dozen is 6 bananas, and they cost 30 rupees.
Find the price of one banana. 30 divided by 6 equals 5.
Divide the money by the price of one banana. 85 divided by 5 equals 17.
85 rupees buys 17 bananas.

options: 17 times 17 plus 18 equals 16 times 16 plus 17 times 3
hints: Each statement is a small sum with a sign. Work out both sides of each one and see whether the sign is true.
Start with 240 divided by 16 and check whether it really is more than 16. Then test the others the same way, multiplying and dividing before adding.

Here is a similar one. Is it true that 5 times 5 plus 6 equals 4 times 4 plus 5 times 3? The left side is 25 plus 6, which is 31. The right side is 16 plus 15, which is 31. Both sides are 31, so it is true.
steps: Is 240 divided by 16 more than 16? It is 15, so no. 240 divided by 16 equals 15.
Is 18 plus 18 divided by 2 equal to 18? Divide first. It comes to 27, so no. 18 plus 18 divided by 2 equals 27.
Now the long statement. Work out its left side. 17 times 17 plus 18 equals 307.
Work out its right side. 16 times 16 plus 17 times 3 equals 307.
Both sides are 307, so 17 times 17 plus 18 equals 16 times 16 plus 17 times 3 is the true one.

EXT_G4_FP_2022_040.q: Number divided by 8: quotient equals 12, remainder equals 0. Same number divided by 3, quotient?
hints: First find the number itself. When there is no remainder, the number is the divisor times the quotient.
Multiply 8 by 12 to get the number. Then divide that number by 3.
Here is a similar one. A number divided by 6 gives quotient 10 and remainder 0, so the number is 6 times 10, which is 60. Dividing 60 by 4 gives 60 divided by 4, which is 15.
steps: The number is the divisor times the quotient. 8 times 12 equals 96.
Now divide the number by 3. 96 divided by 3 equals 32.
The quotient is 32.

EXT_G4_FP_2023_010.q: 1 gross of notebooks costs 2592 rupees. Cost of 68 notebooks?
hints: A gross is a fixed number of things. Find the cost of one notebook first, then the cost of 68.
One gross is 12 dozen, which is 144. Divide 2592 rupees by 144 to find the price of one notebook.
Here is a similar one. 1 gross of pencils costs 720 rupees. One pencil costs 720 divided by 144, which is 5 rupees. So 30 pencils cost 30 times 5, which is 150 rupees.
steps: One gross is 12 dozen. 12 times 12 equals 144.
Find the cost of one notebook. 2592 divided by 144 equals 18.
Multiply by 68. 68 times 18 equals 1224.
68 notebooks cost 1224 rupees.

EXT_G4_FP_2023_017.q: Simplify BODMAS: 178 minus open square bracket, 15 plus 6 of open bracket, 35 minus 2 times 12, close bracket, close square bracket.
hints: This has a bracket inside a bracket. Start with the innermost bracket and work outwards. The word 'of' means multiply.
Begin inside the round bracket, 35 minus 2 times 12. Multiply before you subtract.

Here is a similar one: 100 minus open square bracket, 10 plus 3 of open bracket, 20 minus 2 times 5, close bracket, close square bracket. Inside the round bracket, 2 times 5 equals 10 and 20 minus 10 equals 10. Then 3 of 10 is 30, and 10 plus 30 equals 40. Last, 100 minus 40 equals 60.
steps: Start inside the round bracket and multiply before subtracting: 2 times 12 equals 24, then 35 minus 24 equals 11. 35 minus 2 times 12 equals 11.
The word of means multiply, so 6 of 11 is 6 times 11. 6 times 11 equals 66.
Finish the square bracket. 15 plus 66 equals 81.
Take the square bracket away from 178. 178 minus 81 equals 97.
Working from the innermost bracket outwards, the answer is 97.

EXT_G4_FP_2023_023.q: Compare: 17 times 17 plus 45, blank, 16 times 14 plus 89.
hints: Work out the value of each side on its own. Then compare the two values.
On each side, multiply first and then add. Start with 17 times 17.

Here is a similar one: 12 times 12 plus 10 and 11 times 13 plus 20. The left side is 144 plus 10, which is 154. The right side is 143 plus 20, which is 163. 154 is less than 163, so the sign is less than.
steps: Left side: multiply, then add. 17 times 17 plus 45 equals 334.
Right side: multiply, then add. 16 times 14 plus 89 equals 313.
334 is more than 313, so the sign is greater than.

EXT_G4_FP_2023_039.q: Brackets for BODMAS: 16, plus 24 divided by 4, plus 6 times 2, equals 40.
options: A bracket around 16 plus 24 divided by 4
hints: A bracket changes which part is done first. Test each bracket to see whether the sum becomes 40. It is possible that none of them does.
Take one of the brackets, put it into 16, plus 24 divided by 4, plus 6 times 2, and work it out, bracket first. Do the same for the others.

Here is a similar one. Where does a bracket go to make 10, plus 20 divided by 5, plus 5 times 2, equal to 16? With a bracket around 10 plus 20 you get 30 divided by 5 plus 10, equals 6 plus 10, which equals 16, so that bracket fits. Each bracket must be tested like this.
steps: Try a bracket around 16 plus 24. The bracket is 40, and the sum comes to 22. 40 divided by 4 plus 6 times 2 equals 22.
Try a bracket around 4 plus 6 times 2. The bracket is 16, and 24 divided by 16 does not divide evenly, so this cannot give 40.
Try a bracket around 16 plus 24 divided by 4. The bracket is 22, and the sum comes to 34. 22 plus 6 times 2 equals 34.
No bracket shown makes 40, so the answer is none of these.

EXT_G4_FP_2024_006.q: Where should bracket be: 3 times 25 minus 13 plus 4 equals 40?
hints: A bracket changes which part is done first. Test each bracket and see which one makes the sum equal 40.
Take one of the brackets, put it into 3 times 25 minus 13 plus 4 and work it out, bracket first. See whether it gives 40.

Here is a similar one. Where does a bracket go to make 2 times 15 minus 5 plus 3 equal to 23? Try a bracket around 15 minus 5. Then 2 times 10 plus 3, equals 20 plus 3, which equals 23, so that bracket fits.
steps: Try a bracket around 25 minus 13 and do it first. 25 minus 13 equals 12.
Multiply. 3 times 12 equals 36.
Add. 36 plus 4 equals 40.
The bracket goes around 25 minus 13.

EXT_G4_FP_2024_013.q: Subtract from sum of 2012 and 689 to get 1789?
hints: There are two steps. First find the sum. Then find what must be taken away from it to leave 1789.
Add 2012 and 689 first. The number to take away is the gap between that sum and 1789.
Here is a similar one. What must be subtracted from the sum of 1500 and 250 to get 1200? The sum is 1750. Then 1750 minus 1200 equals 550, so subtract 550.
steps: Find the sum. 2012 plus 689 equals 2701.
Find the gap between the sum and 1789. 2701 minus 1789 equals 912.
You must subtract 912.

EXT_G4_FP_2024_026.q: Simplify: 7 times 7, minus 36, plus 2, plus open curly bracket, open bracket, 8 plus 5 minus 6, close bracket, times 2, close curly bracket.
hints: Brackets come first, then multiplication, then addition and subtraction from left to right.
Start inside the round bracket, 8 plus 5 minus 6. Then multiply that result by 2 to finish the curly bracket. Also work out 7 times 7.

Here is a similar one: 6 times 6, minus 20, plus 1, plus open curly bracket, open bracket, 7 plus 4 minus 5, close bracket, times 3, close curly bracket. The round bracket is 6, and 6 times 3 equals 18. Also 6 times 6 equals 36. Then 36 minus 20 equals 16, 16 plus 1 equals 17 and 17 plus 18 equals 35.
steps: Round bracket first. 8 plus 5 minus 6 equals 7.
Finish the curly bracket. 7 times 2 equals 14.
Do the multiplication at the start. 7 times 7 equals 49.
The sum is now 49 minus 36 plus 2 plus 14. Go from left to right: 49 minus 36 equals 13, then 13 plus 2 equals 15, then 15 plus 14 equals 29. 49 minus 36 plus 2 plus 14 equals 29.
The answer is 29.

EXT_G4_FP_2025_007.q: Use BODMAS to find the value of 192 divided by open bracket, 12 plus open bracket, 72 divided by 8 minus 5, close bracket, times 3, close bracket.
hints: Work from the innermost brackets outwards. Inside each bracket, do division and multiplication before addition and subtraction.
Start with the inner bracket, 72 divided by 8 minus 5. Do the division first, then the subtraction.

Similar example: 100 divided by open bracket, 4 plus open bracket, 18 divided by 3 minus 4, close bracket, times 3, close bracket. Inner bracket: 18 divided by 3 equals 6, then 6 minus 4 equals 2. Next 2 times 3 equals 6, then 4 plus 6 equals 10. Last, 100 divided by 10 equals 10.
steps: Inner bracket first: divide, then subtract. 72 divided by 8 equals 9, and 9 minus 5 equals 4.
In the outer bracket, multiply before adding. 4 times 3 equals 12.
Now add inside the outer bracket. 12 plus 12 equals 24.
Last, divide. The value is 8. 192 divided by 24 equals 8.

EXT_G4_FP_2025_032.q: Bracket for BODMAS: 80 divided by 10, plus 2 times 3, plus 12, equals 17?
options: A bracket around 80 divided by 10 plus 2
hints: A bracket changes which part is done first. Test each bracket and see which one makes the sum equal 17.
Take one of the brackets, put it into 80 divided by 10, plus 2 times 3, plus 12, and work it out, bracket first. See whether it gives 17.

Here is a similar one. Where does a bracket go to make 60 divided by 5, plus 5 times 2, plus 3, equal to 7? Try a bracket around 5 plus 5 times 2. The bracket is 5 plus 10, which is 15. Then 60 divided by 15 plus 3, equals 4 plus 3, which equals 7, so that bracket fits.
steps: Try a bracket around 10 plus 2 times 3. Inside it, multiply first. 10 plus 2 times 3 equals 16.
Divide 80 by the bracket. 80 divided by 16 equals 5.
Add 12. 5 plus 12 equals 17.
The bracket goes around 10 plus 2 times 3.

EXT_G4_FP_2025_033.q: 2 plus 4 plus 6 plus 8 plus 12 plus 16, blank, 8 times 7. Insert sign.
hints: Work out the value of each side on its own. Then compare the two values.
Add up the six numbers on the left. Pairing them into easy tens and twenties makes it quicker. Then work out 8 times 7.
Here is a similar one: 1 plus 3 plus 5 plus 7 plus 9 and 6 times 5. The left side adds up to 25. The right side is 30. 25 is less than 30, so the sign is less than.
steps: Add the left side. 2 plus 4 plus 6 plus 8 plus 12 plus 16, equals 48.
Work out the right side. 8 times 7 equals 56.
48 is less than 56, so the sign is less than.

G4A_OPERATIONS_001.q: A school buys 15 boxes of pencils with 24 pencils in each box. Each of the 12 teachers keeps 8 pencils. The rest are shared equally among 6 classes. How many pencils does each class get?
hints: This story has three parts: how many there are altogether, how many are taken out, and how the rest are shared. Do them in that order.
Find the total number of pencils with 15 times 24. Then find how many the teachers keep with 12 times 8.
A similar one: 10 packets of 12 biscuits make 120. Four children take 5 each, which is 20. The 100 left are put equally on 5 plates, 20 on each.
steps: Total pencils. 15 times 24 equals 360.
Pencils kept by the teachers. 12 times 8 equals 96.
Pencils left for the classes. 360 minus 96 equals 264.
Share them among 6 classes. 264 divided by 6 equals 44.
Each class gets 44 pencils.

G4A_OPERATIONS_002.q: Simplify: 48 divided by open bracket, 10 minus 2 times 3, close bracket, plus 5 times open bracket, 7 minus 4, close bracket.
hints: Brackets come first. Inside a bracket, and outside it, do multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.
Start inside the first bracket: 10 minus 2 times 3. Do the multiplication there before the subtraction.

A similar one: 36 divided by open bracket, 8 minus 2 times 2, close bracket, plus 3 times open bracket, 5 minus 1, close bracket. The brackets are 4 and 4. Then 36 divided by 4 equals 9 and 3 times 4 equals 12, and 9 plus 12 equals 21.
steps: First bracket: multiply before subtracting. 10 minus 2 times 3, equals 10 minus 6, which equals 4.
Second bracket. 7 minus 4 equals 3.
Now divide and multiply. 48 divided by 4 equals 12, and 5 times 3 equals 15.
Add the two results. 12 plus 15 equals 27.
The value is 27.

G4A_OPERATIONS_003.q: Which of these expressions has the smallest value?
options: Open bracket, 30 minus 6, close bracket, divided by 3 plus 2
6 plus 18 divided by open bracket, 3 times 2, close bracket
40 minus 4 times open bracket, 3 plus 5, close bracket
50 divided by open bracket, 2 plus 3, close bracket, plus 1
hints: Work out each expression fully before comparing. Use the order: brackets, then division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction.
Do not judge by the size of the numbers you see. Find each value with care, starting with whatever is inside the brackets.
A similar one: for 20 minus 2 times open bracket, 1 plus 6, close bracket, the bracket is 7, then 2 times 7 equals 14, then 20 minus 14 equals 6. A large first number can still give a small value.
steps: First expression. Open bracket, 30 minus 6, close bracket, divided by 3 plus 2, equals 24 divided by 3 plus 2, which equals 10.
Second expression. 6 plus 18 divided by open bracket, 3 times 2, close bracket, equals 6 plus 18 divided by 6, which equals 9.
Third expression. 40 minus 4 times open bracket, 3 plus 5, close bracket, equals 40 minus 32, which equals 8.
Fourth expression. 50 divided by open bracket, 2 plus 3, close bracket, plus 1, equals 10 plus 1, which equals 11.
The smallest value is 8, which comes from 40 minus 4 times open bracket, 3 plus 5, close bracket.

G4A_OPERATIONS_004.q: A train has 12 coaches with 72 seats in each coach. It leaves the first station with 598 passengers. At the next station 135 passengers get off and 210 get on. Everyone has a seat. How many seats are empty now?
hints: Find two numbers: how many seats the train has, and how many passengers are on it now. The empty seats are the difference.
Seats: 12 times 72. Passengers now: start with 598, take away those who got off, and add those who got on.
A similar one: a bus has 50 seats and 38 riders. Ten get off and 6 get on, so there are 34 riders. Empty seats: 50 minus 34 equals 16.
steps: Seats on the train. 12 times 72 equals 864.
Passengers after the next station. 598 minus 135 plus 210 equals 673.
Empty seats. 864 minus 673 equals 191.
There are 191 empty seats.

G4A_OPERATIONS_005.q: A shopkeeper buys 9 dozen bananas at 4 rupees each. 12 bananas go bad and are thrown away. He sells all the rest at 6 rupees each. How much more money does he get than he paid?
hints: Find the money he paid and the money he got from selling. The question asks for the difference between them.
One dozen is 12, so 9 dozen is 9 times 12 bananas. He pays 4 rupees for every one of them, even the ones that go bad.
A similar one: a man buys 2 dozen eggs at 5 rupees each and pays 120 rupees. Four break, and he sells the other 20 at 8 rupees each for 160 rupees. He gets 40 rupees more than he paid.
steps: Number of bananas bought. 9 times 12 equals 108.
Money paid. 108 times 4 equals 432.
Bananas sold and money received. 108 minus 12 equals 96, and 96 times 6 equals 576.
Difference. 576 minus 432 equals 144.
He gets 144 rupees more than he paid.

G4A_OPERATIONS_006.q: Find the value of 25 times 37 times 4, minus 37 times 99.
hints: Look for numbers that multiply to make a round number. Then look for a number that both parts share.
25 times 4 is 100, so the first part is 37 times 100. Both parts are now a number of 37s.
A similar one: 5 times 13 times 2, minus 13 times 9. Since 5 times 2 equals 10, this is ten 13s minus nine 13s, which leaves one 13. The value is 13.
steps: Multiply 25 and 4 first, because they make 100.
The sum is now a hundred 37s minus ninety-nine 37s. 37 times 100 minus 37 times 99.
That leaves just one 37. 37 times open bracket, 100 minus 99, close bracket, equals 37 times 1.
The value is 37.

G4A_OPERATIONS_007.q: A sweet shop makes 500 laddoos and packs them in boxes of 12. The laddoos left over are shared equally among 4 children. How many laddoos does each child get?
hints: Packing into equal boxes is division, and the laddoos that do not fill a box are the remainder. The children share only the remainder.
Divide 500 by 12. Find how many full boxes there are and how many laddoos are left over.
A similar one: 150 toffees in packets of 8. Eighteen packets use 144 toffees and 6 are left over. Shared between 2 children, each gets 3.
steps: Find the full boxes. 41 times 12 equals 492.
Laddoos left over. 500 minus 492 equals 8.
Share the left-over laddoos among 4 children. 8 divided by 4 equals 2.
Each child gets 2 laddoos.

G4A_OPERATIONS_008.q: Simplify: open curly bracket, 100 minus open square bracket, 60 minus open bracket, 18 plus 12 divided by 3, close bracket, close square bracket, close curly bracket, divided by 2.
hints: Start with the innermost bracket and work outwards: round brackets, then square brackets, then curly brackets.
Inside the round bracket is 18 plus 12 divided by 3. Do the division there before the addition.

A similar one: open curly bracket, 50 minus open square bracket, 30 minus open bracket, 6 plus 8 divided by 2, close bracket, close square bracket, close curly bracket, divided by 5. The round bracket is 6 plus 4, which is 10, then 30 minus 10 equals 20, then 50 minus 20 equals 30, and 30 divided by 5 equals 6.
steps: Round bracket: divide before adding. 18 plus 12 divided by 3, equals 18 plus 4, which equals 22.
Square bracket. 60 minus 22 equals 38.
Curly bracket. 100 minus 38 equals 62.
Divide by 2. 62 divided by 2 equals 31.
The value is 31.

G4A_OPERATIONS_009.q: Asha earns 500 rupees a day and works 6 days every week. Each week she spends 1,800 rupees and saves the rest. How many weeks will she take to save 18,000 rupees?
hints: Find how much she saves in one week first. Then see how many such weeks make the amount she wants.
In one week she earns 6 times 500 rupees. Take away what she spends in a week to get her weekly saving.
A similar one: Ravi earns 200 rupees a day for 5 days, which is 1,000 rupees a week. He spends 600 rupees and saves 400 rupees. To save 2,000 rupees he needs 2,000 divided by 400, which is 5 weeks.
steps: Money earned in a week. 6 times 500 equals 3000.
Money saved in a week. 3000 minus 1800 equals 1200.
Number of weeks needed. 18000 divided by 1200 equals 15.
She will take 15 weeks.

G4A_OPERATIONS_010.q: Simplify: 7 times 8, minus 6 times open bracket, 9 minus 4, close bracket, plus 20 divided by 5 times 2.
hints: Do the bracket first. Then do every multiplication and division, going from left to right. Addition and subtraction come last, also from left to right.
The bracket 9 minus 4 is 5. Now the sum has three parts joined by minus and plus. Work out each part before joining them.

A similar one: 5 times 6, minus 2 times open bracket, 7 minus 3, close bracket, plus 12 divided by 3 times 2. The parts are 30, then 2 times 4 equals 8, then 4 times 2 equals 8. So 30 minus 8 plus 8 equals 30.
steps: Bracket first. 9 minus 4 equals 5.
First two parts. 7 times 8 equals 56, and 6 times 5 equals 30.
Third part, from left to right. 20 divided by 5 times 2, equals 4 times 2, which equals 8.
Join the parts from left to right. 56 minus 30 plus 8 equals 34.
The value is 34.

G4A_OPERATIONS_011.q: A hall has 28 rows with 35 chairs in each row. For a function, 15 rows are taken away completely and 6 more chairs are added to each row that is left. How many chairs are in the hall now?
hints: Two things change: the number of rows and the number of chairs in a row. Find both new numbers before you multiply.
Rows left: 28 minus 15. Chairs in each of those rows: 35 plus 6.
A similar one: 10 rows of 8 chairs. Four rows are removed and 2 chairs are added to each row left. Now there are 6 rows of 10, which is 60 chairs.
steps: Rows left. 28 minus 15 equals 13.
Chairs in each row now. 35 plus 6 equals 41.
Chairs in the hall. 13 times 41 equals 533.
There are 533 chairs in the hall now.

G4A_OPERATIONS_012.q: A farmer has 1,000 mangoes. He fills 25 crates with 2 dozen mangoes in each. He packs the rest in baskets of 50. How many baskets does he need?
hints: Find how many mangoes go into the crates, take them away from the total, and then pack what is left.
One dozen is 12, so 2 dozen is 24 mangoes in each crate. Multiply by 25 crates.
A similar one: 300 oranges. Ten bags hold 1 dozen each, which is 120. The 180 left go into boxes of 30, so 6 boxes are needed.
steps: Mangoes in one crate. 2 times 12 equals 24.
Mangoes in 25 crates. 25 times 24 equals 600.
Mangoes left. 1000 minus 600 equals 400.
Baskets needed. 400 divided by 50 equals 8.
He needs 8 baskets.

G4A_OPERATIONS_013.q: One pair of brackets must be put into 6 plus 4 times 5 minus 3 so that its value becomes 14. Which of these is correct?
options: Open bracket, 6 plus 4, close bracket, times 5 minus 3
6 plus open bracket, 4 times 5, close bracket, minus 3
6 plus 4 times open bracket, 5 minus 3, close bracket
Open bracket, 6 plus 4 times 5, close bracket, minus 3
hints: First find the value with no brackets at all. Then ask whether the brackets need to make the value bigger or smaller, and test each placing.
Without brackets, 4 times 5 is done first, so the value is 6 plus 20 minus 3. Compare this with 14, then try each placing of the brackets.

A similar problem: put brackets in 2 plus 3 times 6 minus 4 to make 8. Without brackets it is 2 plus 18 minus 4, which is 16. Try 2 plus 3 times open bracket, 6 minus 4, close bracket: the bracket gives 2, then 3 times 2 equals 6, then 2 plus 6 equals 8. That placing fits.
steps: Without brackets the value is 23, so the brackets must make it smaller. 6 plus 4 times 5 minus 3 equals 23.
Brackets around 4 times 5, or around 6 plus 4 times 5, change nothing, because the multiplication is done first anyway.
Brackets around 6 plus 4 make the value bigger. Open bracket, 6 plus 4, close bracket, times 5 minus 3, equals 47.

Brackets around 5 minus 3 give 14, so the correct one is 6 plus 4 times open bracket, 5 minus 3, close bracket. 6 plus 4 times open bracket, 5 minus 3, close bracket, equals 6 plus 4 times 2, which equals 14.

G4A_OPERATIONS_014.q: Riya writes 36 divided by 6 plus 3 times 2. She may put one pair of brackets into it, around two or more of the numbers. What is the smallest value she can make?
hints: To make a division give a small result, the number you divide by should be as big as possible. Try every place the brackets can go, not just the first one that helps.
Brackets can go around two numbers or around three numbers. Try brackets starting at the 6: first around 6 plus 3, then around 6 plus 3 times 2.

A similar problem: one pair of brackets in 24 divided by 2 plus 4 times 1. Without brackets it is 12 plus 4, which is 16. With 24 divided by open bracket, 2 plus 4, close bracket, times 1, it is 4. With 24 divided by open bracket, 2 plus 4 times 1, close bracket, it is also 24 divided by 6, which is 4. With open bracket, 24 divided by 2 plus 4, close bracket, times 1, it is 16. The smallest value is 4.
steps: Without brackets the value is 12. 36 divided by 6 plus 3 times 2, equals 6 plus 6, which equals 12.
Brackets around 6 plus 3 make the divisor 9. 36 divided by open bracket, 6 plus 3, close bracket, times 2, equals 4 times 2, which equals 8.
Brackets around 6 plus 3 times 2 make the divisor 12. 36 divided by open bracket, 6 plus 3 times 2, close bracket, equals 36 divided by 12, which equals 3.
Brackets around 36 divided by 6 plus 3 give 18, and the other placings give 12. Open bracket, 36 divided by 6 plus 3, close bracket, times 2, equals 18.
The smallest value Riya can make is 3.

G4A_OPERATIONS_015.q: In 12, box, 6, box, 2, equals 9, each box holds one of the signs plus, minus, times or divide. The usual order of operations is followed. Which signs go in the first box and the second box?
hints: Test each pair of signs, but remember that multiplying and dividing are done before adding and subtracting, wherever they stand.
Try the first choice carefully. In 12 plus 6 divided by 2 the division 6 divided by 2 is done first. What do you get?

A similar problem: 10, box, 8, box, 4, equals 8. Try 10 minus 8 divided by 4: the division comes first, 8 divided by 4 equals 2, then 10 minus 2 equals 8. So the signs are minus then divide. Notice that 10 plus 8 divided by 4 is 10 plus 2, which is 12.
steps: Try plus then divide. The division is done first. 12 plus 6 divided by 2, equals 12 plus 3, which equals 15.
Try minus then divide. The division is done first. 12 minus 6 divided by 2, equals 12 minus 3, which equals 9.
The other two choices give 12 divided by 6 plus 2, which is 4, and 12 minus 6 plus 2, which is 8.
The signs are minus then divide.

G4A_OPERATIONS_016.q: The signs plus, minus and times are each used once to fill the three boxes in 8, box, 2, box, 3, box, 1. The usual order of operations is followed. What is the greatest result that can be made?
hints: Multiplying makes the biggest difference, so think about which two numbers the times sign should sit between. Remember that times is done before plus and minus.
Try putting times in the first box, between 8 and 2. Then decide which of plus and minus should come next to make the result as big as possible.

A similar problem: plus, minus and times once each in 6, box, 3, box, 2, box, 1. With times first: 6 times 3 plus 2 minus 1 equals 19 and 6 times 3 minus 2 plus 1 equals 17. With times in the middle: 6 plus 3 times 2 minus 1 equals 11. With times last: 6 plus 3 minus 2 times 1 equals 7. The greatest is 19.
steps: Put times between the two largest neighbours, 8 and 2, then add the 3 and subtract the 1. 8 times 2 plus 3 minus 1 equals 18.
The other order with times first gives less. 8 times 2 minus 3 plus 1 equals 14.
With times in the middle box the best is 13, and with times in the last box the best is 7. 8 plus 2 times 3 minus 1 equals 13.
The greatest result that can be made is 18.

G4A_OPERATIONS_017.q: A fruit seller has a basket of mangoes. In the morning he sells half of them and 2 more. In the afternoon he sells half of the mangoes that are left and 2 more. Now 8 mangoes are left. How many mangoes were in the basket at the start?
hints: Start from the end and undo each sale. Think carefully about the order: which part of each sale should be undone first?
Before the 2 extra mangoes were sold in the afternoon, there were 8 plus 2 mangoes. That was half of what he had at the start of the afternoon.

A similar problem: a baker sells half of his buns and 3 more, and 5 buns are left. Add back the 3: 5 plus 3 equals 8. That is half, so he started with 8 times 2, which is 16 buns. Check: half of 16 is 8, and 8 minus 3 equals 5.
steps: Undo the afternoon: add back the 2 extra mangoes, then double. Open bracket, 8 plus 2, close bracket, times 2, equals 20.
So 20 mangoes were left after the morning.
Undo the morning in the same way. Open bracket, 20 plus 2, close bracket, times 2, equals 44.
Check: 44 minus 22 minus 2 equals 20, and 20 minus 10 minus 2 equals 8. There were 44 mangoes at the start.

G4A_OPERATIONS_018.q: Asha and Bela have 60 stickers altogether. Asha gives 8 of her stickers to Bela, and now the two girls have the same number of stickers. How many stickers did Asha have at first?
hints: Giving stickers to a friend does not change the total. Start from the end, when both have the same number, and go back to the beginning.
At the end the 60 stickers are shared equally. Find how many each girl has then, and think about what Asha had before she gave some away.
A similar problem: Ravi and Sam have 40 marbles in all. Ravi gives Sam 5 and then they have the same number, 40 divided by 2 equals 20 each. Before giving, Ravi had 20 plus 5, which is 25 marbles.
steps: At the end the two girls have the same number. 60 divided by 2 equals 30.
Asha had given away 8 stickers to reach 30, so add them back. 30 plus 8 equals 38.
Check: Bela had 60 minus 38, which is 22, and 22 plus 8 equals 30.
Asha had 38 stickers at first.

G4A_OPERATIONS_019.q: A farmer packs 500 oranges into boxes that hold 24 oranges each. He fills as many boxes as he can and puts the oranges left over into one more box. How many more oranges does he need to fill that last box completely?
hints: After dividing, think about what the remainder tells you and what the question is really asking for.
Divide 500 by 24 to find how many boxes are full and how many oranges go into the last box.
A similar problem: 100 eggs go into trays of 12. 100 divided by 12 equals 8 remainder 4, so the last tray holds 4 eggs. It needs 12 minus 4, which is 8 more eggs to be full.
steps: Divide to find the full boxes and the oranges left over. 500 equals 24 times 20 plus 20.
So 20 boxes are full and the last box holds 20 oranges.
A box holds 24, so find how many more are needed. 24 minus 20 equals 4.
He needs 4 more oranges to fill the last box.

G4A_OPERATIONS_020.q: Which of these products is the greatest?
hints: Before multiplying, look at what the four pairs have in common. Try the same idea with much smaller numbers to see a pattern.
Add the two numbers in each pair. Then try small pairs with the same total, such as 5 times 5, 4 times 6 and 3 times 7, and see which is biggest.

A similar problem: which is greatest, 10 times 10, 9 times 11 or 8 times 12? Each pair adds up to 20. The products are 100, 99 and 96. The closer together the two numbers are, the bigger the product, so 10 times 10 is greatest.
steps: Each pair of numbers adds up to 100. 47 plus 53, equals 48 plus 52, equals 49 plus 51, which equals 100.
When two numbers have the same total, their product is biggest when the numbers are closest together. Small numbers show this: 5 times 5 equals 25, 4 times 6 equals 24, 3 times 7 equals 21.
Check with the nearest pair. 49 times 51 equals 2499, and 50 times 50 equals 2500.
The greatest product is 50 times 50.

G4A_OPERATIONS_021.q: Which sign must go in the box to make this true? 6 plus 12, box, 3 times 2, equals 12. The usual order of operations is followed.
hints: Test each sign in the box. Each time, do the multiplying and dividing first, then the adding and subtracting from left to right.
Whatever sign goes in the box, 3 times 2 or 12 divided by 3 times 2 is worked out before anything is added to 6. Start by trying divide with care.

A similar problem: 4 plus 10, box, 2 times 3, equals 8. Try minus: the multiplication comes first, 2 times 3 equals 6, then 4 plus 10 minus 6 equals 8. So the sign is minus. With divide it would be 10 divided by 2 times 3, which is 15, and 4 plus 15 equals 19.
steps: Try divide. The dividing and multiplying are done first. 6 plus 12 divided by 3 times 2, equals 6 plus 8, which equals 14.
Try minus. The multiplication is done first. 6 plus 12 minus 3 times 2, equals 6 plus 12 minus 6, which equals 12.
The other two signs give 6 plus 12 plus 6, which is 24, and 6 plus 72, which is 78.
The sign in the box must be minus, the subtract sign.

G4A_OPERATIONS_022.q: In which of these can the brackets be removed without changing the value?
options: 12 minus open bracket, 4 times 2, close bracket
12 minus open bracket, 4 plus 2, close bracket
Open bracket, 12 minus 4, close bracket, times 2
12 divided by open bracket, 4 plus 2, close bracket
hints: Brackets tell you what to do first. They are not needed when the part inside them would be done first anyway.
For each choice, ask: without the brackets, which operation comes first by the order of operations? Is it the same one that is inside the brackets?

A similar problem: in 20 minus open bracket, 3 times 5, close bracket, the multiplication would be done first even without brackets, so 20 minus 3 times 5 equals 5 both ways. In 20 minus open bracket, 3 plus 5, close bracket, the value is 12, but 20 minus 3 plus 5 is 22, so those brackets are needed.
steps: In 12 minus open bracket, 4 times 2, close bracket, the multiplication is done first with or without brackets. 12 minus open bracket, 4 times 2, close bracket, equals 4, and 12 minus 4 times 2 equals 4.
In 12 minus open bracket, 4 plus 2, close bracket, the value changes from 6 to 10 when the brackets go. 12 minus open bracket, 4 plus 2, close bracket, equals 6, and 12 minus 4 plus 2 equals 10.
In open bracket, 12 minus 4, close bracket, times 2, the value changes from 16 to 4, and in 12 divided by open bracket, 4 plus 2, close bracket, it changes from 2 to 5.
The brackets can be removed only in 12 minus open bracket, 4 times 2, close bracket.

G4A_OPERATIONS_023.q: Pencils cost 4 rupees each and pens cost 9 rupees each. Rohit buys 10 of these in all and pays exactly 60 rupees. How many pens does he buy?
hints: Imagine that everything he bought was the cheaper thing. Then see how much the bill goes up each time one of them is swapped for the dearer thing.
If all 10 were pencils, the bill would be 10 times 4 rupees. Find how much more than this Rohit paid.

A similar problem: balls cost 3 rupees and bats cost 8 rupees, and 6 things cost 33 rupees. If all were balls the bill would be 6 times 3, which is 18 rupees. The extra is 33 minus 18, which is 15 rupees. Each bat adds 8 minus 3, which is 5 rupees, so there are 15 divided by 5, which is 3 bats.
steps: If all 10 were pencils, the bill would be 40 rupees. 10 times 4 equals 40.
Rohit paid 20 rupees more than that. 60 minus 40 equals 20.
Each pen costs 5 rupees more than a pencil, so find how many pens make up the extra. 20 divided by 5 equals 4.
Check: 4 pens and 6 pencils cost 36 plus 24, which is 60. He buys 4 pens.

G4A_OPERATIONS_024.q: Kiran had to divide a number by 6. By mistake she multiplied it by 6 and got 432. What answer should she have got?
hints: First find the number Kiran started with by undoing what she did. Then do what she was supposed to do.
Kiran multiplied by 6 and got 432. Undo this by dividing 432 by 6 to find her number.
A similar problem: Mohan had to divide a number by 4 but multiplied by 4 and got 80. His number was 80 divided by 4, which is 20, so he should have got 20 divided by 4, which is 5.
steps: Undo the multiplication to find the number Kiran started with. 432 divided by 6 equals 72.
Now do what she was supposed to do: divide the number by 6. 72 divided by 6 equals 12.
Kiran should have got 12.

PYQ_2016_Q04.q: Insert the proper sign of comparison in the box: 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6 plus 7 plus 8 plus 9, box, 5 times 7.
hints: To choose the sign, you need the value of each side. Work out the left side and the right side separately, and then compare the two numbers.
Add the numbers from 1 to 9. A quick way is to pair them so that each pair makes 10, such as 1 and 9, or 2 and 8. Then work out 5 times 7.
Here is a similar one: compare 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6 with 4 times 6. The left side is 21 and the right side is 24. Since 21 is less than 24, the sign would be less than.
steps: On the left side, pair the numbers to make tens: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6. That is four tens, which is 40, and the 5 in the middle makes 45. 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 5 plus 6 plus 7 plus 8 plus 9, equals 45.
On the right side, multiply. 5 times 7 equals 35.
45 is greater than 35, so the sign in the box is greater than.

PYQ_2016_Q09.q: A bottle contains 150 millilitres of cough syrup. The doctor prescribes 25 millilitres each day. How many days will the cough syrup last for?
hints: The syrup is used up in equal amounts each day. Finding how many equal parts fit into a total is a division problem.
Divide the amount in the bottle, 150 millilitres, by the amount taken each day, 25 millilitres. You can also count up in 25s until you reach 150.
Here is a similar one: a bottle holds 120 millilitres and 30 millilitres is taken each day. 120 divided by 30 equals 4, so that bottle lasts for 4 days.
steps: The bottle holds 150 millilitres and 25 millilitres is taken each day, so divide 150 by 25.
Count up in 25s: 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150. That is 6 lots of 25. 150 divided by 25 equals 6.
The cough syrup will last for 6 days.

PYQ_2016_Q12.q: A fruit seller purchases three baskets of oranges marked A, B and C on the baskets. A contains 16 more oranges than C and B contains 12 more than the sum of A and C. If C contains 22 oranges, how many oranges did the fruit seller purchase?
hints: This is a word problem with several steps. One basket is known, and the other two are described by comparing them with it, so work out the baskets one at a time.
Start with basket C, which has 22 oranges, and use it to find basket A. Basket B depends on A and C together, so leave it until last.

Here is a similar one with three boxes of pencils, P, Q and R. R has 10. P has 5 more than R, so P has 15. Q has 4 more than the sum of P and R, so Q has 15 plus 10 plus 4, which is 29. Altogether there are 15 plus 29 plus 10, which is 54 pencils.
steps: Basket C has 22 oranges. Basket A has 16 more than C. 22 plus 16 equals 38.
Find the sum of A and C. 38 plus 22 equals 60.
Basket B has 12 more than that sum. 60 plus 12 equals 72.
Add all three baskets. 38 plus 72 plus 22 equals 132.
The trap is that B is compared with A and C together, not with just one of them. The fruit seller purchased 132 oranges.

PYQ_2016_Q26.q: A shopkeeper buys 6 gross of pencils. He packs them in boxes which can contain a dozen of these pencils. How many boxes will be packed?
hints: This problem uses two counting words. A dozen is 12 things, and a gross is 12 dozen.
Since one gross is 12 dozen, work out how many dozens there are in 6 gross. Each box holds exactly one dozen.
Here is a similar one: 4 gross of erasers are packed in boxes of a dozen. One gross is 12 dozen, so 4 gross is 4 times 12, which is 48 dozen, and 48 boxes are needed.
steps: One gross is 12 dozen, and a dozen is 12. So one gross is 12 times 12, which is 144 pencils.
6 gross is 6 lots of 144 pencils. 6 times 144 equals 864.
Each box holds a dozen, which is 12 pencils, so divide by 12. 864 divided by 12 equals 72.
A quicker way is to see that 6 gross is 6 times 12, which is 72 dozen, and each dozen fills one box. So 72 boxes will be packed.

PYQ_2016_Q32.q: Which of the following can be the product of star, star, 7 and star, star, 8, where star denotes digits, not necessarily the same?
hints: You cannot know the two numbers, but you can still tell things about their product. Think about what its last digit must be, and about how big or how small it can be.
The numbers end in 7 and 8, so find the last digit of 7 times 8. Then think about how many digits the product of two three-digit numbers can have.

Here is a similar one with two-digit numbers star, 3 and star, 4. Since 3 times 4 equals 12, the product ends in 2. Two two-digit numbers multiply to at least 10 times 10, which is 100, and to less than 100 times 100, which is 10000, so the product has three or four digits. A number like 552 fits, and in fact 23 times 24 equals 552.
steps: The last digit of a product comes from the last digits of the two numbers. 7 times 8 equals 56, so the product must end in 6. That rules out 10552, which ends in 2.
Both numbers have three digits, so each is at least 100. Their product is at least 100 times 100 equals 10000, which has five digits. That rules out 9786, which has only four digits.
Each number is less than 1000, so the product is less than 1000 times 1000, which is 1000000. That rules out 9950006, which has seven digits.
The only number left ends in 6 and is the right size. In fact it can be made. 507 times 608 equals 308256.
Checking the last digit and the number of digits shows that the product can be 308256.

PYQ_2016_Q35.q: Solve using the BODMAS Rule: 6, plus 5 times 4, minus 6 divided by 2.
hints: This sum mixes four operations. Multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction.
Find the multiplication and the division in the sum and work those two out first. Then go from left to right with what is left.
Here is a similar one: 8, plus 3 times 6, minus 10 divided by 5. First 3 times 6 equals 18 and 10 divided by 5 equals 2. Then 8 plus 18 equals 26, and 26 minus 2 equals 24.
steps: Do the multiplication first. 5 times 4 equals 20.
Do the division next. 6 divided by 2 equals 3.
The sum is now 6 plus 20 minus 3. Go from left to right: 6 plus 20 equals 26, and then 26 minus 3 equals 23. 6 plus 20 minus 3 equals 23.
So 6, plus 5 times 4, minus 6 divided by 2, equals 23.

PYQ_2017_Q09.q: Where should the bracket be put to make the following equation true: 5 times 7 plus 3 minus 10 equals 40?
hints: Brackets change the order of a sum, because whatever is inside a bracket is done first. The task is to find the bracket that makes the left side come to 40.
Try each way of placing the bracket in turn. Work out the bracket first, and then follow the usual order: multiplication before addition and subtraction. See which one gives 40.

Here is a similar one: where should the bracket go to make it true that 4 times 6 plus 2 minus 5 equals 27? Without a bracket the left side is 24 plus 2 minus 5, which is 21. With a bracket around 6 plus 2 it becomes 4 times 8 minus 5, and 32 minus 5 equals 27. So the bracket goes around 6 plus 2.
steps: Without any bracket, 5 times 7 equals 35 is done first, and 35 plus 3 minus 10 equals 28. That is not 40.
A bracket around 5 times 7, or around 5 times 7 plus 3, does not change the order, so the result is still 28.
A bracket around 7 plus 3 minus 10 comes to 0, and 5 times 0 equals 0.
A bracket around 7 plus 3 comes to 10. Then 5 times 10 equals 50, and 50 minus 10 equals 40. 5 times open bracket, 7 plus 3, close bracket, minus 10, equals 40.
The bracket has to make the addition happen before the multiplication. So the bracket goes around 7 plus 3.

PYQ_2017_Q29.q: Simplify using the BODMAS Rule: 9 minus 3 times 2 plus open bracket, 2 times 4 minus 15 divided by 3, close bracket.
hints: This sum has a bracket and four operations. The bracket is done first, and inside it the usual order still applies: multiply and divide before you add or subtract.
Start inside the bracket with 2 times 4 and 15 divided by 3, and then subtract. After that, look outside the bracket and do the multiplication before going from left to right.

Here is a similar one: 20 minus 4 times 3 plus open bracket, 2 times 5 minus 8 divided by 4, close bracket. Inside the bracket, 2 times 5 equals 10 and 8 divided by 4 equals 2, so the bracket is 10 minus 2, which is 8. Outside, 4 times 3 equals 12. Then 20 minus 12 equals 8, and 8 plus 8 equals 16.
steps: Start inside the bracket, with the multiplication and the division: 2 times 4 equals 8 and 15 divided by 3 equals 5.
Finish the bracket. 8 minus 5 equals 3.
Outside the bracket, multiply. 3 times 2 equals 6.
The sum is now 9 minus 6 plus 3. Go from left to right: 9 minus 6 equals 3, and then 3 plus 3 equals 6. 9 minus 6 plus 3 equals 6.
The trap is to do 9 minus 3 first, or to take the bracket away instead of adding it. The answer is 6.

PYQ_2017_Q39.q: What is 11 times 7, plus 13 times 7, minus 7 times 6, plus 2 times 7?
hints: Every part of this sum is a number multiplied by 7. When the same number is multiplied each time, you can collect the other numbers first and multiply by 7 just once.
Either work out each of the four products and then add and subtract from left to right, or count how many 7s there are altogether: 11 sevens and 13 sevens, take away 6 sevens, and 2 sevens more.
Here is a similar one: 9 times 5, plus 6 times 5, minus 5 times 4, plus 1 times 5. Count the fives: 9 plus 6 minus 4 plus 1 equals 12. Then 12 times 5 equals 60.
steps: Work out each product: 11 times 7 equals 77, 13 times 7 equals 91, 7 times 6 equals 42 and 2 times 7 equals 14.
Now go from left to right: 77 plus 91 equals 168, then 168 minus 42 equals 126, then 126 plus 14 equals 140. 77 plus 91 minus 42 plus 14 equals 140.
As a quick check, there are 11 plus 13 minus 6 plus 2, which is 20 sevens altogether. 20 times 7 equals 140.
Both ways give the same result, so the answer is 140.

PYQ_2018_Q05.q: According to the BODMAS Rule, which of the following is correct?
options: Open bracket, 18 plus 7, close bracket, divided by 7, equals 19
hints: Each choice is a little sum with a result. To test one, work out its left side yourself in the BODMAS order and see whether you get the number shown.
Take the statements one at a time. Do brackets first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction. Compare your result with the number after the equals sign.
Here is a similar one: is it true that 3 plus 4 times 5 comes to 35? Multiply first: 4 times 5 equals 20, and then 3 plus 20 equals 23. So that statement is not true; 35 comes from adding first.
steps: In 2 times 7 minus 5, multiply first: 2 times 7 is 14, and 14 minus 5 equals 9. The statement says 4, so it is not true.
In 5 plus 5 times 25, multiply first: 5 times 25 is 125, and 5 plus 125 equals 130. The statement says 250, so it is not true.
In open bracket, 18 plus 7, close bracket, divided by 7, the bracket is 25, and 25 divided by 7 is 3 with 4 left over. The statement says 19, so it is not true.
